title: Regulations on Alcohol, Controlled Substances, and Public Decorum
summary: Egypt maintains a balanced framework that respects personal liberties within authorized venues while strictly enforcing public sobriety, religious sanctity, and public order.

sections.heading: Alcohol Consumption & Sale (Law No. 63 of 1976)
content: Licensed Venues Only: Alcohol consumption is legally restricted to licensed establishments, including hotels, tourist restaurants, and certified lounges/bars.

Public Sobriety & Open Containers: Drinking alcohol in public spaces, on streets, or in private vehicles is strictly illegal. Public drunkenness constitutes a breach of public order and carries immediate detention.

Holy Month of Ramadan & Islamic Holidays: The sale and service of alcohol are strictly restricted to non-Egyptian passport holders in licensed tourist facilities during Ramadan and major Islamic religious holidays.
Age Limit: The legal drinking and purchasing age for alcohol in Egypt is 21 years.

sections.heading: Narcotics and Prescription Medications
content: Zero Tolerance Narcotics Laws: Possession, distribution, or consumption of illegal narcotics (including cannabis/hashish, synthetic drugs, and opiates) is treated as a major crime under Law No. 182 of 1960. Sentences range from multi-year hard labor to capital punishment for smuggling.

Controlled Prescription Drugs: Specific prescription medications (e.g., Tramadol, Xanax, Codeine, and Adderall) are classified as controlled substances. Travellers bringing restricted medications into Egypt must carry an official doctor's certificate and an legalized prescription matching the exact quantity.
